new_theorem: Crossed-recycler escalation. In a width-at-most-three no-balanced poset, suppose x lessdot y, a||x,y, and the exact external witness union of (x,a) and (y,a) is the crossed pair {c,u} with c||x, c<a,y and x,a<u, y||u. Let L be fresh distinguishers of (c,x) beyond a and the five-core, and R the analogous fresh distinguishers of (y,u). Then L and R are nonempty. Every shared recycler r in L intersect R satisfies r||x,y,a and c<r<u, and all shared recyclers form a chain. If L union R has only one vertex r, then none of the old core distinguishes (a,r), so the one-distinguisher theorem forces at least two further outside distinguishers. Thus a crossed exact-two heavy-edge state cannot close on a five- or six-vertex two-channel loop in a hypothetical counterexample.
